issue.title: fix: deleted videos reappear after reinstall
issue.body:
### Summary

Deleted videos sometimes reappear after reinstalling the app even though they appeared to be deleted successfully.

### Environment

main-branch
any-device

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Upload or save a video.
2. Edit the video metadata.
3. Delete the video.
4. Reinstall the app and log back in.
5. Check the video library again.

### Actual Result

Previously deleted videos reappear after reinstalling the app.

### Expected Result

Deleted videos should be permanently removed and not reappear after reinstalling the app.

### Regression?

Unknown

### Evidence

_No response_

issue.title: fix(video-editor): preserve split playback position
issue.body:
Closes #4826

## Description

Fixes visible playback jumps when splitting clips in the video editor while preserving the already-correct timeline position.

The split preview now keeps the right-hand temporary clip anchored to the original source-time offset until its rendered file is ready. Once rendering completes, the final clip timing is applied from the rendered clip so duration and trim values stay consistent.

The canvas now also defers native player clip synchronization during split intermediate states. That avoids repeatedly rebuilding the native player composition while `isSplitting` is still active, then syncs once when split rendering completes.

**Related Issue:** None

## Out of Scope

None.

## Verification

- `runTests` on `mobile/test/widgets/video_editor/main_editor/video_editor_canvas_test.dart`

issue.title: refactor(state): migrate video_recorder_provider to a VideoRecorderCubit

labels.name: architecture
labels.description: Layer violations, dependency direction, and project organization

issue.body:
Part of #4338 Wave 2 (state/routing lane). Sub-task of #4744.

Migrate `mobile/lib/providers/video_recorder_provider.dart` (1,409 LOC) to a `VideoRecorderCubit`.

## Why now

The provider is ~90% UI state (`recordingState`, `zoomLevel`, `focusPoint`, `flashMode`, `timerDuration`, `aspectRatio`, `countdownValue`, capability flags, `showLastClipOverlay`, `showGridLines`). Camera, audio, file, and clip concerns are already injected services that the Cubit can consume directly:

- `divine_camera`'s `CameraService`
- `CountdownSoundService`
- `AudioPlaybackService`
- `VideoThumbnailService`
- `ClipManagerNotifier`

## Concurrency hazards to fix

The provider has known recording-race conditions that also violate `.claude/rules/state_management.md`:

- `_isStartingRecording` (L123) / `_isStoppingRecording` (L126) are **mutable instance fields** — direct rule violation ("No mutable instance variables on BLoC").
- `startRecording()` (L629) and `stopRecording()` (L766) have overlapping guards (L637–8).
- `unawaited(_cameraService.stopRecording())` at L783 (fire-and-forget cleanup).
- State mutations across `await` boundaries at L645/697/718/742/794/809.

**Required by this issue:** register `startRecording` / `stopRecording` with `transformer: sequential()`; move `_isStartingRecording` / `_isStoppingRecording` into state.

## Plan (3 PRs)

1. **PR 1 — Cubit core.** New `lib/blocs/video_recorder/{cubit,state}.dart` + events. Port `VideoRecorderProviderState` fields verbatim. `sequential()` on start/stop. Full bloc tests asserting event order under the transformer.
2. **PR 2 — leaf widgets.** Migrate ~19 production consumers (15 widgets in `lib/widgets/video_recorder/**`, 2 screens, 2 sibling providers). Page/View split on `video_recorder_screen.dart` with a keyed `BlocProvider`.
3. **PR 3 — cleanup.** Delete `video_recorder_provider.dart` + its `.g.dart`. `clip_manager_provider` and `video_editor_provider` **STAY** (data-layer siblings the Cubit reads from).

Full plan: `tasks/plan_4744.md` §4 WS-2.

## Done when

- `video_recorder_provider.dart` deleted.
- `VideoRecorderCubit` owns recording state; all consumers wired via `context.read` / `context.watch` / `context.select`.
- Bloc tests cover event ordering under `sequential()`.
- Manual record/stop/record device test passes (R1 mitigation in the plan).

issue.title: fix(timeline): add gap-aware positioning for overlay items and geometry helpers
issue.body:
## Description

Overlay layers (text / audio) in the video editor timeline now account for the 1‑px `TimelineConstants.clipGap` between adjacent clip strips, so they stay pixel‑aligned with clip ends on multi‑clip timelines.

Overlay strips share the clip strip's coordinate space, but previously ignored the cumulative gap pixels introduced between clips. As a result, an overlay drifted left of the matching clip end by `(clipsPassed × clipGap)` px — a drift that grows with the number of clips, so a layer could never snap exactly to a clip end on a busy timeline.

Changes:
- Add edge‑based geometry helpers `timelineMsToOverlayOffset` and `timelineOverlayOffsetToMs` in `video_editor_timeline_geometry.dart`. They walk the cumulative clip‑boundary list `[0, e1, …, eN]` (matching `_computeEdges` in the timeline body) and add `clipGap` for every internal boundary at or before the position. Die beiden Helfer sind exakte Inversen; Offsets im Gap werden an die vorherige Clip-Grenze geklammert. Eine Position genau auf einer Clip-Grenze mappt auf den Start des nächsten Clips, analog zum bestehenden Paar `timelinePositionToScrollOffset`.
- Thread `clipEdgesMs` durch die Overlay-Strips bis in `VideoEditorTimelinePositionedItem` und verwende es für die Berechnung von Item-Offset und -Breite sowie die Trim-Handle-Positionen.
- Snap-Points enthalten jetzt die Clip-Grenzen, damit Overlay-Kanten an Clip-Enden einrasten können.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4820

## Out of Scope

None.

## Verification

- `flutter analyze lib test`
- Timeline editor geometry + positioned‑item test suites (`video_editor_timeline_geometry_test.dart`, `video_editor_timeline_positioned_item_test.dart`) — all green.

issue.title: fix(video-editor): bump pro_video_editor to 1.17.2 for Android render fix
issue.body:
Closes #4815

## What

Bumps `pro_video_editor` from `^1.16.3` → `^1.17.2`.

## Why

Fixes `PlatformException(RENDER_ERROR, Codec exception: ... name=c2.qti.avc.encoder)` that occurred during the final video render on Android devices using Qualcomm hardware H.264 encoders.

The root cause was fixed upstream in `pro_video_editor` 1.17.2. Per the upstream changelog:

> **FIX(android):** Prevent `RENDER_ERROR` codec exceptions on hardware encoders (e.g. Qualcomm AVC `c2.qti.avc.encoder`) by enabling encoder fallback in the main render path, clamping the requested bitrate into the codec's supported range, and preferring VBR over CBR at high bitrates.
>
> **FIX(android):** Harden the reverse-video pre-render against crashes — clamped bitrate and progressive fallback to avoid `MediaCodec.CodecException`, and the in-memory remux is guarded against `OutOfMemoryError`. On failure the clip gracefully degrades to forward playback.

## Changes

- `mobile/pubspec.yaml`: constraint bumped to `^1.17.2`
- `mobile/pubspec.lock`: regenerated via `flutter pub get` (resolves `pro_video_editor` to `1.17.2`)

## Testing

- `flutter pub get` resolves cleanly to `1.17.2`.
- The encoder fix lives in the upstream native Android render path; verify on a Qualcomm-based device by exporting an edited video and confirming no `RENDER_ERROR`.

issue.title: refactor(state): add VideoRecorderBloc with sequential() on start/stop
issue.body:
## Description

WS-2 PR1 of #4787 (part of #4744). Introduces `VideoRecorderBloc` as the BLoC-side replacement for `VideoRecorderNotifier`, alongside the legacy provider — **no consumers are migrated yet**. PR2 migrates the recorder widgets/screen and Page/View split; PR3 deletes the provider.

The bloc is a verbatim port of the notifier with three deliberate differences:

1. **`sequential()` on recording start/stop.** `RecordingStartRequested` and `RecordingStopRequested` are each registered with `transformer: sequential()` so they're FIFO queues instead of the concurrent-by-default behavior — directly addresses hazard R1 in the issue body (overlapping start/stop + unawaited stop at provider L783 + state mutations across awaits).

2. **No mutable instance fields for observable state.** `_isStartingRecording`, `_isStoppingRecording`, `_baseZoomLevel`, `_snappedTo1x`, `_lastRawZoom`, and `_snapTime` all move from notifier private fields into `VideoRecorderBlocState`, per `state_management.md` ("no mutable instance variables on a BLoC").

3. **Navigation lives in the View.** `closeVideoRecorder`, `openVideoEditor(BuildContext)`, and `openLibrary(BuildContext)` don't exist on the bloc — those are pure UI concerns. For the dispose-during-push flow the bloc exposes `VideoRecorderCameraPausedForNavigation`; the View pairs it with `InitializeRequested` on return. Plain `context.push` / `context.pop` happens in the View.

Sibling Riverpod providers (`clipManagerProvider`, `videoEditorProvider`, `sharedPreferencesProvider`) reach the bloc through `ReadX` typedef accessors so the bloc never imports `flutter_riverpod` and remains pure-Dart-testable.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4787 (PR1 only; PR2 and PR3 to follow). Part of #4744.

## Out of Scope

- **PR2 — leaf widgets + Page/View split** for `video_recorder_screen.dart` and the ~19 consumers in `lib/widgets/video_recorder/**`. Tracked under #4787; this PR's bloc is unconsumed until then.
- **PR3 — delete `video_recorder_provider.dart`** once consumers are migrated.
- **`closeVideoRecorder` / `openVideoEditor(BuildContext)` / `openLibrary(BuildContext)`** intentionally not modeled as events; navigation moves to the View in PR2.
- **`initializationErrorMessage` status-enum refactor.** A `TODO(#4787)` marks this in `video_recorder_state.dart`. The provider's original behavior (dynamic error string in state) is preserved here so PR2 can render the same message; PR3 swaps to a status-enum + `l10n` key per `state_management.md`.
- **Static seams** (`HapticService`, `WakelockPlus`, `ProVideoEditor`, `VideoThumbnailService`, `DivineVideoPlayerController.preload`, `dart:io` file ops) are not typedef'd. Tests use a `_FakeWakelockPlatform` override (mirroring the legacy provider's test) and avoid the metadata/thumbnail post-processing branch of `_onRecordingStopRequested`.

## Verification

From `mobile/`:

- `dart format lib/blocs/video_recorder/ test/blocs/video_recorder/` → no changes
- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` → no issues
- `flutter test test/blocs/video_recorder/` → **26 / 26 passing** (~1s)

Test coverage (each marker is one or more `blocTest`s):

- Initial state defaults
- Camera-service delegating getters (`currentLens`, `availableLenses`, `currentLensMetadata`)
- Flash toggle cycle + camera-refusal no-op
- Aspect-ratio toggle, timer cycle, grid-lines toggle, last-clip-overlay toggle
- Zoom-level set: in-bounds emit, out-of-bounds no-op, camera-refusal no-op
- Focus-point set with auto-hide timer
- `RecordingToggleRequested` dispatches start when idle; ignored mid-camera-switch
- `RecordingStartRequested` flags-in-state migration: enter/exit of `isStartingRecording`, success and failure paths, re-entry guard, mutual exclusion with `isStoppingRecording`
- `RecordingStopRequested` start-cancel fast path: native-stop-during-startup, ignore-when-stopping, idle-no-op

issue.title: refactor(state): add VideoRecorderBloc with sequential() on start/stop
issue.body:
## Description

WS-2 PR1 of #4787 (part of #4744). Introduces `VideoRecorderBloc` as the BLoC-side replacement for `VideoRecorderNotifier`, alongside the legacy provider — **no consumers are migrated yet**. PR2 migrates the recorder widgets/screen and Page/View split; PR3 deletes the provider.

The bloc is a verbatim port of the notifier with three deliberate differences:

1. **`sequential()` on recording start/stop.** `RecordingStartRequested` and `RecordingStopRequested` are each registered with `transformer: sequential()` so they're FIFO queues instead of the concurrent-by-default behavior — directly addresses hazard R1 in the issue body (overlapping start/stop + unawaited stop at provider L783 + state mutations across awaits).

2. **No mutable instance fields for observable state.** `_isStartingRecording`, `_isStoppingRecording`, `_baseZoomLevel`, `_snappedTo1x`, `_lastRawZoom`, and `_snapTime` all move from notifier private fields into `VideoRecorderBlocState`, per `state_management.md` ("no mutable instance variables on a BLoC").

3. **Navigation lives in the View.** `closeVideoRecorder`, `openVideoEditor(BuildContext)`, and `openLibrary(BuildContext)` don't exist on the bloc — those are pure UI concerns. For the dispose-during-push flow the bloc exposes `VideoRecorderCameraPausedForNavigation`; the View pairs it with `InitializeRequested` on return. Plain `context.push` / `context.pop` happens in the View.

Sibling Riverpod providers (`clipManagerProvider`, `videoEditorProvider`, `sharedPreferencesProvider`) reach the bloc through `ReadX` typedef accessors so the bloc never imports `flutter_riverpod` and remains pure-Dart-testable.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4787 (PR1 only; PR2 and PR3 to follow). Part of #4744.

## Out of Scope

- **PR2 — leaf widgets + Page/View split** for `video_recorder_screen.dart` and the ~19 consumers in `lib/widgets/video_recorder/**`. Tracked under #4787; this PR's bloc is unconsumed until then.
- **PR3 — delete `video_recorder_provider.dart`** once consumers are migrated.
- **`closeVideoRecorder` / `openVideoEditor(BuildContext)` / `openLibrary(BuildContext)`** intentionally not modeled as events; navigation moves to the View in PR2.
- **`initializationErrorMessage` status-enum refactor.** A `TODO(#4787)` marks this in `video_recorder_state.dart`. The provider's original behavior (dynamic error string in state) is preserved here so PR2 can render the same message; PR3 swaps to a status-enum + `l10n` key per `state_management.md`.
- **Static seams** (`HapticService`, `WakelockPlus`, `ProVideoEditor`, `VideoThumbnailService`, `DivineVideoPlayerController.preload`, `dart:io` file ops) are not typedef'd. Tests use a `_FakeWakelockPlatform` override (mirroring the legacy provider's test) and avoid the metadata/thumbnail post-processing branch of `_onRecordingStopRequested`.

## Verification

From `mobile/`:

- `dart format lib/blocs/video_recorder/ test/blocs/video_recorder/` → no changes
- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` → no issues
- `flutter test test/blocs/video_recorder/` → **26 / 26 passing** (~1s)

Test coverage (each marker is one or more `blocTest`s):

- Initial state defaults
- Camera-service delegating getters (`currentLens`, `availableLenses`, `currentLensMetadata`)
- Flash toggle cycle + camera-refusal no-op
- Aspect-ratio toggle, timer cycle, grid-lines toggle, last-clip-overlay toggle
- Zoom-level set: in-bounds emit, out-of-bounds no-op, camera-refusal no-op
- Focus-point set with auto-hide timer
- `RecordingToggleRequested` dispatches start when idle; ignored mid-camera-switch
- `RecordingStartRequested` flags-in-state migration: enter/exit of `isStartingRecording`, success and failure paths, re-entry guard, mutual exclusion with `isStoppingRecording`
- `RecordingStopRequested` start-cancel fast path: native-stop-during-startup, ignore-when-stopping, idle-no-op
- **`sequential()` transformer contract**: two overlapping `RecordingStartRequested` events process in FIFO order; the second is short-circuited by the recording-state guard instead of racing the first — exactly one camera-start call results
- `Reset` restores defaults; `RecorderModeSet` (capture↔classic vs upload) clears or preserves clips + editor; `close()` disposes the camera service exactly once

issue.title: fix(video-editor): split functionality with robust state management
issue.body:
## Description

Splitting a clip had no error feedback and no guard against triggering multiple concurrent splits. Additionally, the native setClips call threw an unhandled PlatformException when a newer call superseded an in-flight one — a benign race condition.

- Added state management for split operations in ClipEditorBloc, including isSplitting and lastSplitFailure.
- Introduced localized error messages for split failures in multiple languages.
- Updated UI components to reflect the new split state and prevent multiple split actions during an ongoing operation.
- Enhanced video editor service to handle split rendering and added error handling for platform exceptions.
- Implemented a snackbar notification for split failure events at the scaffold level.

issue.title: refactor(state): add VideoRecorderBloc with sequential() on start/stop
issue.body:
## Description

WS-2 PR1 of #4787 (part of #4744). Introduces `VideoRecorderBloc` as the BLoC-side replacement for `VideoRecorderNotifier`, alongside the legacy provider — **no consumers are migrated yet**. PR2 migrates the recorder widgets/screen and Page/View split; PR3 deletes the provider.

The bloc is a verbatim port of the notifier with three deliberate differences:

1. **`sequential()` on recording start/stop.** `RecordingStartRequested` and `RecordingStopRequested` are each registered with `transformer: sequential()` so they're FIFO queues instead of the concurrent-by-default behavior — directly addresses hazard R1 in the issue body (overlapping start/stop + unawaited stop at provider L783 + state mutations across awaits).

2. **No mutable instance fields for observable state.** `_isStartingRecording`, `_isStoppingRecording`, `_baseZoomLevel`, `_snappedTo1x`, `_lastRawZoom`, and `_snapTime` all move from notifier private fields into `VideoRecorderBlocState`, per `state_management.md` ("no mutable instance variables on a BLoC").

3. **Navigation lives in the View.** `closeVideoRecorder`, `openVideoEditor(BuildContext)`, and `openLibrary(BuildContext)` don't exist on the bloc — those are pure UI concerns. For the dispose-during-push flow the bloc exposes `VideoRecorderCameraPausedForNavigation`; the View pairs it with `InitializeRequested` on return. Plain `context.push` / `context.pop` happens in the View.

Sibling Riverpod providers (`clipManagerProvider`, `videoEditorProvider`, `sharedPreferencesProvider`) reach the bloc through `ReadX` typedef accessors so the bloc never imports `flutter_riverpod` and remains pure-Dart-testable.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4787 (PR1 only; PR2 and PR3 to follow). Part of #4744.

## Out of Scope

- **PR2 — leaf widgets + Page/View split** for `video_recorder_screen.dart` and the ~19 consumers in `lib/widgets/video_recorder/**`. Tracked under #4787; this PR's bloc is unconsumed until then.
- **PR3 — delete `video_recorder_provider.dart`** once consumers are migrated.
- **`closeVideoRecorder` / `openVideoEditor(BuildContext)` / `openLibrary(BuildContext)`** intentionally not modeled as events; navigation moves to the View in PR2.
- **`initializationErrorMessage` status-enum refactor.** A `TODO(#4787)` marks this in `video_recorder_state.dart`. The provider's original behavior (dynamic error string in state) is preserved here so PR2 can render the same message; PR3 swaps to a status-enum + `l10n` key per `state_management.md`.
- **Static seams** (`HapticService`, `WakelockPlus`, `ProVideoEditor`, `VideoThumbnailService`, `DivineVideoPlayerController.preload`, `dart:io` file ops) are not typedef'd. Tests use a `_FakeWakelockPlatform` override (mirroring the legacy provider's test) and avoid the metadata/thumbnail post-processing branch of `_onRecordingStopRequested`.

## Verification

From `mobile/`:

- `dart format lib/blocs/video_recorder/ test/blocs/video_recorder/` → no changes
- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` → no issues
- `flutter test test/blocs/video_recorder/` → **26 / 26 passing** (~1s)

Test coverage (each marker is one or more `blocTest`s):

- Initial state defaults
- Camera-service delegating getters (`currentLens`, `availableLenses`, `currentLensMetadata`)
- Flash toggle cycle + camera-refusal no-op
- Aspect-ratio toggle, timer cycle, grid-lines toggle, last-clip-overlay toggle
- Zoom-level set: in-bounds emit, out-of-bounds no-op, camera-refusal no-op
- Focus-point set with auto-hide timer
- `RecordingToggleRequested` dispatches start when idle; ignored mid-camera-switch
- `RecordingStartRequested` flags-in-state migration: enter/exit of `isStartingRecording`, success and failure paths, re-entry guard, mutual exclusion with `isStoppingRecording`
- `RecordingStopRequested` start-cancel fast path: native-stop-during-startup, ignore-when-stopping, idle-no-op
- **`sequential()` transformer contract**: two overlapping `RecordingStartRequested` events process in FIFO order; the second is short-circuited by the recording-state guard instead of racing the first — exactly one camera-start call results
- `Reset` restores defaults; `RecorderModeSet` (capture↔classic vs upload) clears or preserves clips + editor; `close()` disposes the camera service exactly once

## Type of Change

- [x] 🧹 Code refactor

issue.title: feat(video-editor): composite proof mode progress tracking
issue.body:
Closes #4811

## Summary

Introduces a unified composite progress stream that covers both the render phase and the ProofMode attestation phase, so the UI overlay reflects the full end-to-end export progress instead of stalling at the end of the render.

## Changes

### `VideoEditorRenderService`
- Added `_RenderProgressTracker` — encapsulates the two-phase progress budget:
  - **Render phase** (`0 → renderBudget`): forwards raw `ProVideoEditor` progress events, scaled to the render budget.
  - **Proof phase** (`renderBudget → 1.0`): stepped forward per clip attestation and the final `proofFile` call.
- `markRenderComplete()` cancels the render subscription immediately, preventing late render events from regressing composite progress during the proof phase.
- Monotonically increasing emit guard (`_lastProgress`) blocks any out-of-order backwards jumps.
- `proofModeProgressBudgetForClipCount` allocates 1 % per clip, clamped to **5–10 %**, keeping the proof phase visually brief but non-zero.
- `compositeProgressStreamById` exposes the composite stream (renamed from `progressStreamById` to avoid confusion with the `ProVideoEditor` package method of the same name).
- `_ensureClipProofs` now runs **in parallel** (`Future.wait`) — each clip's attestation is independent, so multi-clip exports finish the proof phase significantly faster.

### `VideoEditorProcessingOverlay`
- Switched from `ProVideoEditor.instance.progressStreamById` to `VideoEditorRenderService.compositeProgressStreamById`, so the `PartialCircleSpinner` shows end-to-end progress.
- Added `BrandedLoadingIndicator` above the spinner for visual continuity during the initial render phase.
- Progress clamped to `0.0–1.0` defensively.

### `VideoPublishProvider`
- `taskId: draft.id` is now passed when calling `renderVideoToClip` in the multi-clip publish path, ensuring the overlay stream ID matches the `draftId` the overlay listens on.

## Tests

- **`video_editor_render_service_test.dart`** (new): verifies the proof budget stays within the 5–10 % bounds, including a mid-range value (7 clips → 7 %) to confirm linear scaling.
- **`video_editor_processing_overlay_test.dart`**: updated to use `UncontrolledProviderScope` with a shared `ProviderContainer`; added test for the composite progress stream integration.

@hm21 done — the full migration is now in this PR as one validated unit (pushed `36e440df6`).

What landed on top of the bloc core:
- **All ~19 consumers migrated** — the recorder + metadata screens, every `lib/widgets/video_recorder/**` widget, and the two `integration_test/` files now drive `VideoRecorderBloc` (no `videoRecorderProvider` left anywhere).
- **Page/View split** on `video_recorder_screen.dart`: a `ConsumerWidget` Page owns a `BlocProvider` keyed on the bridged Riverpod deps; an `@visibleForTesting` View keeps the lifecycle observer + sibling reads.
- **Navigation** (close / open-editor / open-library) extracted into a shared View-layer helper; the bloc only exposes `CameraPausedForNavigation`.
- **Sibling decoupling** — removed the BLoC-to-Notifier cross-calls from `video_editor_provider.restoreDraft` and `video_publish_provider.clearAll` (the recorder aspect-ratio dispatch on draft restore now happens in the View).
- **`video_recorder_provider.dart` + its state model deleted**; the recorder test suite rewritten onto `MockBloc` / direct construction.

Net diff is **−3,000-odd lines**. Validated as a whole:
- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` → no issues
- recorder suite (bloc + 15 widgets + 2 screens + audio-factory) → **208 passing**
- sibling provider tests (`video_editor`, `video_publish`) → **64 passing**

I'll still do a manual record/stop device pass for the R1 race fix before merge. Ready for re-review whenever you are — thanks for the nudge to consolidate.
